facts.statement: Shamosaurus was a herbivorous basal ankylosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Shamosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal ankylosaurid ankylosaur from Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian stage) deposits of Höövör, Mongolia.

facts.statement: A Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered the first ankylosaur skeleton in the Lower Cretaceous of Mongolia in 1977.
facts.quote: In 1977, a Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered the skeleton of an unknown ankylosaurian at the Hamrin-Us site in Dornogovi Province.

facts.statement: Tatyana Tumanova named and described the species Shamosaurus scutatus in 1983.
facts.quote: In 1983, Tatyana Tumanova named and described the type species Shamosaurus scutatus.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil dates to about 115 million years ago and comes from the Dzunbain Formation.
facts.quote: Shamosaurus is known from the holotype PIN N 3779/2, collected from the Dzunbain Formation, equivalent to the Khukhtekskaya Formation and dating from the Aptian-Albian, about 115 million years old.

facts.statement: The known fossils include a complete skull, lower jaws, and a partial postcranial skeleton with armor.
facts.quote: It consists of a complete skull, lower jaws and partial postcranial skeleton with armor.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Shamosaurus to be 5 meters long and weigh 2 tonnes in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its body length at 5 metres (16 ft), its weight at 2 tonnes (2.2 short tons).

facts.statement: Mark Holtz estimated Shamosaurus to be 7 meters long in 2012.
facts.quote: In 2012 Holtz gave a higher estimation of 7 meters (23 ft).

facts.statement: The osteoderms on Shamosaurus's skull roof were not pronounced or separated into distinct head tiles.
facts.quote: The osteoderms on the skull roof are not very pronounced nor separated as distinctive caputegulae, head tiles.

facts.statement: Shamosaurus had short, slightly rounded horns at the rear corners of its skull.
facts.quote: The squamosal horns on the rear skull corners are short and slightly rounded.

facts.statement: Shamosaurus possessed a sharp, toothless upper beak that angled forward.
facts.quote: The upper beak was sharp and obliquely appending to the front. The beak lacked any teeth.

facts.statement: Shamosaurus had two cervical halfrings, each with six segments, that protected its neck.
facts.quote: The armour of Shamosaurus contained two cervical halfrings with six segments each, protecting the neck.

facts.statement: Tumanova classified Shamosaurus within the family Ankylosauridae and established the subfamily Shamosaurinae.
facts.quote: Tumanova placed Shamosaurus in the Ankylosauridae. She also named a Shamosaurinae, a group of basal ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: A 2014 phylogenetic analysis by Victoria Arbour identified Shamosaurus as the sister species of Gobisaurus.
facts.quote: In 2014, Arbour recovered an evolutionary tree in which Shamosaurus was the sister species of Gobisaurus.

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest Shamosaurus belongs to Shamosaurinae or is a more derived ankylosaurid than Gobisaurus.
facts.quote: In phylogenetic analyses by Xing et al. (2024), Shamosaurus is recovered as a member of Shamosaurinae or as an ankylosaurid, more derived than Gobisaurus.

facts.statement: Shamosaurus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The generic name is derived from Mandarin sha mo, 'sand desert', the Chinese name for the Gobi.
